_about: Kirsopp Lake’s footnotes to his Greek text (G the Codex Mediceus Laurentianus (the Vossian manuscript); g the long recension; L the Latin version (Grosseteste); A the Armenian; S the Syriac; C the Sahidic; B the Berlin papyrus), and in "refs" the passages of Scripture he prints in the margin (with the digital file’s own reference, "urn"). The digital file has only the Greek pages, so the footnotes Lake prints under his English translation on the facing pages are not here. "at" is the verse the note or reference stands in ("title": the title above the greeting). Greek inside a note is in Beta Code, as in the digital file (so h(mw=n = ἡμῶν), and the file has slips in the notes’ English and Greek (those checked against Lake’s printed page are corrected, with the evidence in "fixed"). From First1KGreek (Open Greek and Latin), CC BY-SA 4.0.

notes.note: o( om. G, but the parallelism with h( peristera/ shows that this is only an accident.
notes.fixed: paralleliam sith → parallelism with (letters misread; both Internet Archive scans of Lake’s printed page (apostolicfathers01lake, TheApostolicFathersV1) read “the parallelism with”); shoss → shows (w read as s; both Internet Archive scans of Lake’s printed page (apostolicfathers01lake, TheApostolicFathersV1) read “shows”)

notes.note: The use of the Latin words is remarkable: dese/rtwr= desertor, depo/sita=deposita, and a)/kkepta=accepta.
notes.fixed: sords → words (w read as s; both Internet Archive scans of Lake’s printed page (apostolicfathers01lake, TheApostolicFathersV1) read “the Latin words”)

notes.note: dia\ th\n proseuxh/n G. dia\ th=s proseuxh=s Lg.
a)nasta/sei GL, ai)th/sei through your intercession gA.
The combination of singular and plural is very strange. L makes all singular, A all plural. The punctuation given is in the main Lightfoot's, but even so the sentence is unsatisfactory.

refs.fixed: 3, 17 → 8, 17 (a misread 8 (Matthew 8:17, “he took our sicknesses”, beside “bear the sicknesses of all”); both Internet Archive scans of Lake’s printed page (apostolicfathers01lake, TheApostolicFathersV1) read “Mt. 8, 17”)

at 4:2 in the digital file → 4:3 (the Internet Archive scan of Lake’s printed page (TheApostolicFathersV1) prints “I Tim. 6, 2” in the margin of the line that begins 4:3 (δούλους καὶ δούλας, the slaves of 1 Timothy 6:2))
2, 1 → 2, 4 (a misread 4 (2 Timothy 2:4, pleasing the one who enlisted him); both Internet Archive scans of Lake’s printed page (apostolicfathers01lake, TheApostolicFathersV1) read “II Tim. 2, 4”)
